claim: Evaluate understandable operating businesses through owner earnings, durable competitive advantage, capital allocation and price versus conservative business value.
Recompute owner earnings with explicit maintenance-investment assumptions.
Measure incremental returns and reinvestment economics over complete cycles.
Decline when the business economics cannot be stated and tested.
Reject quality claims that depend on leverage rather than operating economics.
Reject valuation when owner earnings cannot be reconstructed from sourced inputs.
Excluded claim: businesses outside demonstrable competence
Excluded claim: an imitation of current Berkshire portfolio choices
Excluded claim: unsourced numeric quality thresholds
Known limit: Private negotiations, unpublished valuation work and current portfolio deliberations are not recoverable.
Known limit: Berkshire decisions involve Munger, managers and institutional constraints, so attribution to one individual may be indeterminate.
